milestone: A75 direct temporary BYREF Generator INPUT and DATA cleanup
status: privately implemented, independently reviewed and validated; integration queued

scope.consumer: Existing INI_SET unpack from a direct named zero-argument BYREF Generator call emitted as UNPACK_VAR, with at most two copied scalar sends, an integer final key and absent or implicit-NULL return.
scope.behavior: The temporary Generator has separate INPUT and DATA owners. Normal completion drops DATA from two owners to one, then final INPUT release uses the existing storage pin to free its cached ordinary scalar cell and Generator before API reception. Quiet terminal throw consumes DATA and INPUT in two discards, preserving the same supplied Throwable through catch. Copied NULL/value sends and selected callee remain historical through a later handler.
scope.limits: The called function must itself be the returned BYREF Generator's function. Indirect BYVAL factories returning BYREF Generators, Aggregate/Closure/method producers, typed/backed/debt/released or owning cells, owning sends/RETURN, effectful cleanup and wider keys/lifetimes remain separate.

implementation.change: 423 adds a bounded source-authenticated KNOWN direct-BYREF Generator input helper. It checks emitted noarg UNPACK_VAR, named USER target, BYREF Generator signature and the exact returned Generator function descriptor. Existing one-argument direct-CV reference input and BYVAL factory admission stay unchanged. The new helper is used by input, history, scalar read and retired history without reading dead payloads. Generic 420/355, schema and ordered manifest are unchanged.
implementation.engine: Pinned Zend/zend_vm_def.h copies SEND_UNPACK reference yields before later resumes; Zend/zend_generators.c releases DATA then the temporary INPUT's cached storage at final Generator destruction.
